BiblicalUsage: This word is the pit the deceiver digs for others. Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good things in possession. One verse, one rule: the trap takes its maker.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the proverb is a promise as well as a warning, for the one who leads others astray falls where he dug, and I hold that God keeps the upright.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
